correctness.rationale: For all p,q in [0,1]^2, the homogenized two-site TV equals d(1+|1-t|)/2. After swapping measures and complementing coordinates one may take d>0, t in [1,2]. Marginal TV supplies max(|a|,|b|), and the event 11 supplies |va+ub|. Oppositely signed increments yield TV>=d. With both increments nonnegative, h=max(a/d,b/d) gives TV/d>=max(h,1-(2-t)h)>=1/(3-t). Restoring complements gives the exact stated pooled-mean lower bound; (2-w)(1+w)<=9/4 gives c=8/9. The known epsilon family gives ratio 8/(9-3epsilon)->8/9. The exact arithmetic checker independently tested 35,828 rational quadruples and four ratios. No finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The first lead paper explicitly conjectures the sharp c=8/9 and establishes only c>=about 0.0115, while already constructing the two-coordinate asymptotic upper witness. The second lead paper improves a general-alphabet lower constant to >0.1489 but still calls determination of the sharp constant open. Their statements and the inspected relevant mathematical arguments do not imply the matching finite n=2 lower bound or the pooled-mean bound. Searches of published mathematical records for close aliases/ratios/parameters did not find covering claims. Priority uncertainty remains, and the sharpness example is explicitly attributed to Kontorovich.

value.rationale: This settles the smallest nontrivial fixed-dimension case of the precise sharp-constant 8/9 conjecture formulated by Kontorovich. The optimum had previously only an n=2 upper obstruction and weak dimension-free lower constants. Its complete two-coordinate proof covers all four real Bernoulli parameters with no dominance assumptions and includes a motivated pooled-mean-sensitive lower bound. It is meaningful as an exact natural finite-dimensional boundary, while not claiming to settle n>=3 or arbitrary alphabets.
